answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring each participant to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or access valuable tasks. The ledger links that stake to the agent’s history, so splitting into a hundred fresh identities does not multiply influence: each must fund its own bond, and cheating risks losing it. A mirror of past behavior can guide counterparties, but the signal is the bonded stake, not a claimed persona. An attacker must tie up real capital for the whole voyage and accept forfeiture if caught.
